title: Inverse Galois at Prime Degree: |Gal(Xˡ−p)| = ℓ·(ℓ−1) = |AGL(1,ℓ)| for Every Prime ℓ and Prime p
description: Extracts the general prime-degree consequence of the parent's coprime pin. The parent proved |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| = n·φ(n) exactly whenever gcd(n,φ(n)) = 1 (the metacyclic ceiling |Gal| ≤ n·φ(n) meets the coprime lower bound n·φ(n) ∣ |Gal|). At a PRIME degree ℓ the coprimality hypothesis is automatic: φ(ℓ) = ℓ−1, and a prime ℓ never divides the smaller positive number ℓ−1, so Nat.Coprime ℓ (ℓ−1) holds (coprime_self_totient_of_prime, via Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd). Hence the coprime pin applies at EVERY prime degree, giving the closed form gal_card_prime_degree: |Gal(Xˡ−p/ℚ)| = ℓ·(ℓ−1) for every prime ℓ and prime p — uniform in p, with no genericity hypothesis. This is the order of the one-dimensional affine group AGL(1,ℓ) = 𝔽ₗ ⋊ 𝔽ₗˣ, the largest solvable transitive subgroup of Sₗ, and it subsumes the parent instances 2 (ℓ=2), 6 (ℓ=3), 20 (ℓ=5) in a single statement. The companion gal_index_in_symm proves |Gal|·(ℓ−2)! = ℓ!, i.e. Gal(Xˡ−p) sits inside Sₗ with index exactly (ℓ−2)!; for ℓ ≥ 5 this index exceeds 1, so the Galois group of the irreducible Xˡ−p is a PROPER subgroup of the full symmetric group — radical polynomials are never Sₗ-generic at prime degree ≥ 5. The instance gal_card_septic_eq_42 gives |Gal(X⁷−p/ℚ)| = 42 = |AGL(1,7)|, the next case beyond the parent's quintic 20, where the factorial bound |Gal| ∣ 7! = 5040 is hopelessly loose. 4 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

mathlibDependencies.description: φ(p) = p − 1 for a prime p; reduces the parent's n·φ(n) pin to the closed form ℓ·(ℓ−1) and exposes the coprimality target Nat.Coprime ℓ (ℓ−1).
For a prime ℓ, Nat.Coprime ℓ n ↔ ¬ ℓ ∣ n; turns the coprimality of ℓ with ℓ−1 into the non-divisibility ℓ ∤ (ℓ−1), discharged because 0 < ℓ−1 < ℓ.
(n+1)! = (n+1)·n!; used twice to factor ℓ! = ℓ·(ℓ−1)·(ℓ−2)! and identify the index (ℓ−2)! of Gal inside Sₗ.
Parent lemma: gcd(n,φ(n)) = 1 ⟹ |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| = n·φ(n). The exact coprime pin specialised here to every prime degree, where coprimality is automatic.

overview.historicalContext: The parent chain pins the order of the metacyclic Galois group of $X^n-p$ exactly whenever $\gcd(n,\varphi(n)) = 1$: the unconditional metacyclic ceiling $|\mathrm{Gal}| \le n\,\varphi(n)$ meets the coprime lower bound $n\,\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$, giving $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^n-p/\mathbb{Q})| = n\,\varphi(n)$ for every prime $p$. The parent extracted only the single quintic instance $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^5-p)| = 20$. The natural question is whether a uniform closed form holds across a whole family of degrees rather than case by case.
overview.problemStatement: Show that at every PRIME degree $\ell$ the coprimality hypothesis is automatic, and deduce the uniform closed form $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^\ell-p/\mathbb{Q})| = \ell(\ell-1) = |\mathrm{AGL}(1,\ell)|$ for every prime $\ell$ and every prime $p$. Locate this group inside the symmetric group $S_\ell$ by computing its index.
overview.proofStrategy: (1) Coprimality for free: $\varphi(\ell) = \ell - 1$ (Nat.totient_prime), and a prime $\ell$ cannot divide the strictly smaller positive number $\ell - 1$, so by Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd we get $\mathrm{Coprime}\,\ell\,(\ell-1)$ — the hypothesis of the parent's coprime pin, with $\ell \ge 2$ from Nat.Prime.two_le and the divisibility contradiction closed by omega. (2) Closed form: feed this into gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime to get $|\mathrm{Gal}| = \ell\,\varphi(\ell)$, then rewrite $\varphi(\ell) = \ell - 1$. (3) Index in $S_\ell$: writing $\ell = m+2$, factor $\ell! = (m+2)! = (m+2)(m+1)\,m! = \ell(\ell-1)(\ell-2)!$ via two applications of Nat.factorial_succ and ring, giving $|\mathrm{Gal}|\,(\ell-2)! = \ell!$. (4) Instantiate $\ell = 7$: $7\cdot 6 = 42$.
keyInsights: **Prime degree makes coprimality automatic.** The parent's exact pin $|\mathrm{Gal}| = n\,\varphi(n)$ requires $\gcd(n,\varphi(n)) = 1$, a hypothesis that must be checked. At a prime degree $\ell$ it is free: $\varphi(\ell) = \ell-1$ and consecutive integers $\ell, \ell-1$ are always coprime, so the closed form holds at $\ell = 2,3,5,7,11,13,\dots$ with no per-degree verification.

**$X^\ell-p$ realises the affine group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,\ell)$ uniformly.** $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^\ell-p/\mathbb{Q})| = \ell(\ell-1)$ for every prime $\ell$ and every prime $p$ — the order of the one-dimensional affine group $\mathbb{F}_\ell \rtimes \mathbb{F}_\ell^\times$ over the prime field, independent of $p$. This single statement subsumes the cubic $6$, quintic $20$, and septic $42$.

**The Galois group is a PROPER subgroup of $S_\ell$ for $\ell \ge 5$.** The index $[S_\ell : \mathrm{Gal}] = \ell!/(\ell(\ell-1)) = (\ell-2)!$ exceeds $1$ once $\ell \ge 5$. So despite $X^\ell-p$ being irreducible and separable, its Galois group is never the full symmetric group at prime degree $\ge 5$ — radical polynomials are the antithesis of $S_\ell$-generic, sitting in the largest solvable transitive subgroup $\mathrm{AGL}(1,\ell)$ instead.

**The factorial bound is useless at prime degree.** For $\ell = 7$ the symmetric-group bound only gives $|\mathrm{Gal}| \mid 5040$, leaving dozens of divisors open; the metacyclic ceiling pins it at exactly $42$. The gap $\ell(\ell-1) \ll \ell!$ widens super-exponentially, so the cyclotomic ceiling — not the $S_\ell$ bound — is what determines the order.

sections.title: Overview: prime degree forces the affine group
sections.summary: Header docstring and imports. Recalls the parent's coprime pin |Gal(Xⁿ−p)| = n·φ(n) (gcd(n,φ(n)) = 1) and frames the prime-degree specialisation, where coprimality is automatic, giving the uniform closed form ℓ·(ℓ−1) = |AGL(1,ℓ)|. Imports the verified parent lemma gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime.

sections.title: Part I — Coprimality for free at prime degree
sections.summary: Proves coprime_self_totient_of_prime: for a prime ℓ, Nat.Coprime ℓ (φ ℓ). Rewrites φ(ℓ) = ℓ−1 (Nat.totient_prime) and ℓ.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd, then derives a contradiction from ℓ ∣ (ℓ−1) via Nat.le_of_dvd and omega (a prime never divides a smaller positive number).

sections.title: Part II — The prime-degree closed form |Gal(Xˡ−p)| = ℓ·(ℓ−1)
sections.summary: Proves gal_card_prime_degree by feeding the automatic coprimality into the parent's gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime (with ℓ ≥ 2 from Nat.Prime.two_le) and rewriting φ(ℓ) = ℓ−1. The result ℓ·(ℓ−1) is the order of AGL(1,ℓ), uniform in p.

sections.title: Part III — Index (ℓ−2)! inside the symmetric group
sections.summary: Proves gal_index_in_symm: |Gal|·(ℓ−2)! = ℓ!. Writes ℓ = m+2 and factors ℓ! = ℓ·(ℓ−1)·(ℓ−2)! via two Nat.factorial_succ rewrites and ring. For ℓ ≥ 5 the index (ℓ−2)! > 1, so Gal is a proper subgroup of Sₗ.

sections.title: Part IV — The septic witness |Gal(X⁷−p)| = 42 = |AGL(1,7)|
sections.summary: Proves gal_card_septic_eq_42 by instantiating gal_card_prime_degree at ℓ = 7, yielding |Gal(X⁷−p/ℚ)| = 42 for every prime p — the next case beyond the parent's quintic 20, where the factorial bound |Gal| ∣ 5040 is far too loose.

conclusion.summary: Specialised the parent's coprime pin to prime degree, where coprimality of ℓ with φ(ℓ) = ℓ−1 is automatic, yielding the uniform closed form |Gal(Xˡ−p/ℚ)| = ℓ·(ℓ−1) = |AGL(1,ℓ)| for every prime ℓ and prime p — one statement subsuming the cubic 6, quintic 20, and septic 42. Located the group inside Sₗ with index exactly (ℓ−2)!, showing it is a proper subgroup for ℓ ≥ 5: radical polynomials are never Sₗ-generic at prime degree. 4 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Upgrades the parent's single quintic instance to an infinite family in one theorem. The Galois group of every prime-degree radical extension is now pinned to the affine group AGL(1,ℓ), the canonical solvable transitive subgroup of Sₗ — a concrete, uniform-in-p answer to the inverse-Galois realisation question at prime degree. The index computation (ℓ−2)! quantifies exactly how far these groups sit below the generic Sₗ.
openQuestions: Upgrade the order equality |Gal(Xˡ−p)| = ℓ(ℓ−1) to an explicit group isomorphism Gal(Xˡ−p/ℚ) ≅ AGL(1,ℓ) = 𝔽ₗ ⋊ 𝔽ₗˣ, identifying the radical Cₗ kernel and the cyclotomic 𝔽ₗˣ quotient as the semidirect factors.
Determine the prime-power degree case |Gal(X^{ℓᵏ}−p)|: here gcd(ℓᵏ, φ(ℓᵏ)) = ℓ for k ≥ 2, so the coprime pin fails and the order drops below the metacyclic ceiling ℓᵏ·φ(ℓᵏ); find the exact value.

Characterise the composite non-prime degrees n with gcd(n,φ(n)) = 1 (the coprime pin still applies, e.g. n = 15) versus those with gcd(n,φ(n)) > 1 (n = 4, 8, 9, ...), giving a complete map of where ℓ(ℓ−1)-style closed forms hold.
